messages:
Marta Ruiz: Quick sync tiny forms decision: inline microcopy below fields vs top-level error summary in the dense Console. Many collapsed sections; keyboard-first.
Devin Chen: Inline is best for mapping, but in dense rows it causes layout shift. I prefer tiny inline markers + a single summary toast on submit with anchors.
Ellie Wong: Accessibility: if we hide helpers visually in compact mode, use aria-describedby and aria-invalid so SRs read the message even when helper is collapsed.
Priya Singh: Asterisk vs explicit 'Required'? Asterisk is compact but ambiguous. I vote explicit small 'Required' for clarity on first item in a group.
Marta Ruiz: What about space tradeoff? Could we show a tiny dot/asterisk and sr-only 'Required' copy? Automation can rely on data-required attribute.
Devin Chen: data-required="true" is a good call. For errors: show terse inline label ("Required", "Invalid") but keep full helper in sr-only or revealed on focus.
Ellie Wong: Also add focus move to the first invalid field on submit and open containing accordion. Use role="alert" or aria-live on error nodes to announce after focus. Avoid fragile setTimeout hacks.
Marta Ruiz: Destructive confirmation patterns: typed-confirm for irreversible data (DB drops, audit deletion). Modal+undo for routine single-item deletes. Token should be a single lowercase word, monospace.
Priya Singh: Example copy: "Type delete-pool to permanently remove pool 'payments-prod' (id: 1357). This action cannot be undone." Keep token lowercase no punctuation.
Devin Chen: Toast collision: autosave/info toasts vs validation errors. Rule: one toast visible at a time. Priority queue: error > undo > info. Queue lower priority toasts.
Ellie Wong: QA styling nit: compact input focus ring must be >=3px and meet contrast in dim themes.
Marta Ruiz: Action items: design to produce two mock variants: (A) compact marker + summary toast with anchor links + ARIA, (B) persistent tiny 'Required' postfix + inline helpers. Include SR announcement tests and keyboard-only flows.
